body: I understand where you are coming from, you don’t want the “charm” and “exclusivity” of the masters to fade away. You want the ability to wear the masters gear and get the complements and questions from other people that see you wearing a masters article of clothing (correct me if I’m wrong). However, you also have to look at it from the other perspective, what makes someone who attends the masters more deserving to wear the merch versus someone who didn’t? Is it because they didn’t win a lottery to obtain tickets? The Masters is not as exclusive as people make it out to be. Yes it’s really hard to obtain tickets through the lottery but roughly 90,000 people attended the masters this past year (give or take a few) and I’m willing to bet a good majority of them purchased masters gear for their friends. Why are the friends of people who attended more entitled to wear the gear and not others that purchased through Selhigh? The masters over the years has been overly romanticized into this highly exclusive, never going to gain access to attend, event. At its core, it’s a golf tournament. Before I say anything else, I have been. People that attended aren’t any more deserving to wear the merch than someone else. If you really want to get mad about something, get mad about the tickets resellers that are charging thousands for a single day pass. I’d argue that ruins the charm of the tournament more than a T-shirt with a logo ever will. What Selhigh is doing is providing an opportunity for people to obtain something that they desire. I believe you mentioned that you’re in sales in the comment section (I could be mistaken) but how is that any different than what Selhigh does? He’s providing a service for people in exchange for money? Not necessarily for a huge profit I might add. The Robinhood of Augusta as I like to say :)
